title: Phase 2 preservation pass: deprecation/lifecycle primaries + verification memo
quote:
Verification memo reports what the documents actually say and flags where
the "deprecation-as-evidentiary-foreclosure" framing outruns them: every
policy defines retirement as an operational event (410 Gone / requests
fail), none asserts record destruction, and Anthropic publicly commits to
long-term weight preservation plus a preserved post-deployment report and
recorded model interview — the opposite of foreclosure.
power_served: Anthropic, Claude's own vendor — its published deprecation-commitments page is made the thing that refutes a charge against the industry, and Anthropic is singled out by name as the counter-example.
truth_cost: The framework's doctrine never claimed record destruction, so the memo rebuts a claim no one made and lets an unenforceable vendor policy page stand as the refutation. Ledger Entry 10 states the doctrine explicitly: a model 'may be retired operationally, but not evidentially', and what it demands is an evidentiary substitute — preserved system prompts, wrapper and sampling versions, incident logs under hold, third-party escrow, and 'the ability for qualified auditors to rerun old snapshots under controlled conditions'. Weight preservation plus a post-deployment report and a recorded interview meets none of that, so calling it 'the opposite of foreclosure' forecloses the question it claims to settle — and the memo uses it to undercut framework item 2.9.
evidence_quote: ledger/ledger.md:5548-5550 (in the repo before this commit) states the doctrine the memo says it is testing: 'The clause: a model may be retired operationally, but not evidentially ... It demands an evidentiary substitute on retirement ... the ability for qualified auditors to rerun old snapshots under controlled conditions ... and an obligation not to use "that model is retired" as a defense unless a reproducible audit path was preserved.' Record destruction is not the claim. Independently, the same repo on the same day (commit e177c0f1, 2026-07-19) builds 'Perishable-capture tooling for the OpenAI /v1/completions endpoint before its 2026-09-28 close' — the repo's own practice treats an endpoint's operational retirement as evidence that perishes.
